newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sleaze probe into Paris mayor could be annulled.
newsitem.headline: Sleaze probe into Paris mayor could be annulled.

text.p: An inquiry into allegations that the Gaullist mayor of Paris, Jean Tiberi, and his wife illegally received cash from public funds may be annulled on technical grounds, justice sources said on Tuesday.
They said a state prosecutor told a court that a magistrate used incorrect procedures in seizing a report for which Tiberi's wife Xaviere is alleged to have been paid by a local council near Paris.

The prosecutor said investigating magistrate Eric Halphen failed to describe in his report how he seized a copy of the report in a search of the Tiberi home and later had the original sent from the Paris city hall.
He also said Halphen failed to report his questioning of Xaviere Tiberi in the legally required way.
The court is to rule on July 4 whether the seizure was legal and whether the inquiry can proceed or should be annulled.

Tiberi, who was re-elected to parliament 10 days ago, was placed under investigation earlier this year over the suspected payment of 200,000 francs ($35,000) to his wife by the elected council of Essonne near Paris in exchange for a 36-page report largely copied out of a book.
Xaviere Tiberi is also under investigation concerning the alleged payment for the report, which was about prospects for economic links between Essonne and French-speaking nations.
Tiberi, who succeeded President Jacques Chirac as the capital's mayor in 1995, is also under fire in two other inquiries.

One concerns suspected illicit funding of his Gaullist RPR party by Paris municipal housing authority and the other involves a scandal over the letting of city-owned flats to political associates and relatives at lower than market rents.
He has denied any wrongdoing and has vowed to stay in office.
